division_answers.answer:
### [THUD] TRANSPORTATION, HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, AND RELATED AGENCIES
Bottom line: HUD’s FY2026 housing-related funding is spread across multiple accounts for affordable housing, rental assistance, and homelessness services, and no clean division-wide total is available because the figures mix account totals with suballocations and advance/previously appropriated amounts.
Key buckets:
- Affordable housing supply and public housing operations: Public Housing Fund $8,319,393,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_1]] for 2026 public housing operations and capital/management activities, including $4,687,393,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_2]] for the operating fund formula, $337,000,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_3]] for need-based shortfall support, and $3,200,000,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_4]] for the capital fund formula; HOME investment partnerships program $1,250,000,000 [[num:src_thud_79d43909_fd59_4e62_90b8_b6ef05e3467a_1]]; Section 811 project rental assistance $287,000,000 [[num:src_thud_853b7fb5_28ff_4aa9_be82_2ff235743a46_1]].
- Rental assistance: tenant-based rental assistance $34,438,557,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_1]] plus $4,000,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_2]] previously appropriated and $4,000,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_3]] available on October 1, 2026; of the sums appropriated, $34,957,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_4]] is for renewals of expiring section 8 tenant-based annual contributions contracts; project-based rental assistance $18,143,000,000 [[num:src_thud_f1b2363f_5009_4e7f_a53a_19d7a641efa5_1]] plus $400,000,000 [[num:src_thud_f1b2363f_5009_4e7f_a53a_19d7a641efa5_2]] previously appropriated and $400,000,000 [[num:src_thud_f1b2363f_5009_4e7f_a53a_19d7a641efa5_3]] available on October 1, 2026.
- Homelessness services: Homeless Assistance Grants $4,417,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_1]] under title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act, including $290,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_2]] for the emergency solutions grants program and $4,010,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_3]] for the continuum of care program and rural housing stability assistance; the Act also directs non-competitive 12-month renewals for expiring Homeless Assistance Grants / continuum of care projects in early 2026; youth homelessness demonstration projects $107,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e4156bb6_ba90_4d3d_895c_fabbe74b30cd_1]], with up to $25,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e4156bb6_ba90_4d3d_895c_fabbe74b30cd_2]] for youth homelessness system improvement grants and up to $10,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e9ada4e4_1b7e_4403_af35_2e53e7ea4854_2]] for technical assistance.

final_answer:
### [THUD] TRANSPORTATION, HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, AND RELATED AGENCIES
Bottom line: HUD’s FY2026 housing-related funding is spread across multiple accounts for affordable housing, rental assistance, and homelessness services, and no clean division-wide total is available because the figures mix account totals with suballocations and advance/previously appropriated amounts.
Key buckets:
- Affordable housing supply and public housing operations: Public Housing Fund $8,319,393,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_1]] for 2026 public housing operations and capital/management activities, including $4,687,393,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_2]] for the operating fund formula, $337,000,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_3]] for need-based shortfall support, and $3,200,000,000 [[num:src_thud_9841cfd4_18e8_4504_8843_461e06569ba5_4]] for the capital fund formula; HOME investment partnerships program $1,250,000,000 [[num:src_thud_79d43909_fd59_4e62_90b8_b6ef05e3467a_1]]; Section 811 project rental assistance $287,000,000 [[num:src_thud_853b7fb5_28ff_4aa9_be82_2ff235743a46_1]].
- Rental assistance: tenant-based rental assistance $34,438,557,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_1]] plus $4,000,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_2]] previously appropriated and $4,000,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_3]] available on October 1, 2026; of the sums appropriated, $34,957,000,000 [[num:src_thud_4a3a0d30_b7b3_442e_8ee2_d6e04108d60d_4]] is for renewals of expiring section 8 tenant-based annual contributions contracts; project-based rental assistance $18,143,000,000 [[num:src_thud_f1b2363f_5009_4e7f_a53a_19d7a641efa5_1]] plus $400,000,000 [[num:src_thud_f1b2363f_5009_4e7f_a53a_19d7a641efa5_2]] previously appropriated and $400,000,000 [[num:src_thud_f1b2363f_5009_4e7f_a53a_19d7a641efa5_3]] available on October 1, 2026.
- Homelessness services: Homeless Assistance Grants $4,417,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_1]] under title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act, including $290,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_2]] for the emergency solutions grants program and $4,010,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e0672ad1_4356_43e9_afad_46ca77ac5d8b_3]] for the continuum of care program and rural housing stability assistance; the Act also directs non-competitive 12-month renewals for expiring Homeless Assistance Grants / continuum of care projects in early 2026; youth homelessness demonstration projects $107,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e4156bb6_ba90_4d3d_895c_fabbe74b30cd_1]], with up to $25,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e4156bb6_ba90_4d3d_895c_fabbe74b30cd_2]] for youth homelessness system improvement grants and up to $10,000,000 [[num:src_thud_e9ada4e4_1b7e_4403_af35_2e53e7ea4854_2]] for technical assistance.
